candidates: When computing inter-atomic distances from `NeighborList` output, never call `atoms.get_distances()` on the returned neighbor indices — it ignores periodic-image offsets and yields incorrect distances for atoms near cell boundaries. Instead, capture both return values with `j_indices, offsets = nl.get_neighbors(i)` and compute distances explicitly: `d = atoms.positions[j_indices] + offsets @ atoms.cell - atoms.positions[i]; distances = np.linalg.norm(d, axis=1)`. See `ase/calculators/emt.py` for the canonical usage pattern in this codebase.

When constructing a `NeighborList` for pair-counting analysis (e.g., RDF or coordination statistics), pass `bothways=True` so every pair is enumerated in both directions. Adjust the normalization formula to account for this double-counting rather than manually halving the raw counts.

When using `NeighborList` for geometric analysis that produces a histogram or distribution (e.g., RDF), iterate directly over neighbors and accumulate counts — do not build an intermediate dense N×N distance matrix. The NeighborList approach correctly handles multiple periodic images of the same atom within the cutoff radius, whereas a distance matrix can represent only the shortest image and forces O(N²) memory allocation.

When filtering neighbor indices returned by `nl.get_neighbors()` by atomic species, use NumPy boolean masking throughout: `mask = atoms.numbers[j_indices] == target_element; j_indices, offsets = j_indices[mask], offsets[mask]`. Apply the same mask to both the index array and the corresponding offsets array to keep them in sync.

When using `np.bincount` to accumulate histogram counts into a fixed-size array, always pass `minlength=nbins + 1` and slice the result to `[:nbins + 1]`, e.g. `np.bincount(indices, minlength=nbins + 1)[:nbins + 1]`. This guarantees the output has exactly the expected length even when the largest index falls short of `nbins`.

Tests for functions that accept element-type arguments or implement partial/element-filtered analysis (e.g., partial RDFs, coordination counts) must include at least one test case covering a two-element or multi-element system, not only homogeneous single-element cases.
